Commentary.Commentary: So, England have finally declared. They looked to up the ante after the break and they did manage to add some quick runs. The visitors managed to pull things back a little with Chase, as he was their pick of the bowlers today bagging four wickets. The away side has a mammoth task on its hands as they have to cut down a huge deficit and it won't be easy against a star-studded England bowling attack especially with the ball which will do a lot under lights. Join us for the Windies' innings in a while.

OUT! LBW! Alastair Cook has to walk back. Roston Chase was the one who was dead sure to take the review and it has paid off. He sends in a quicker delivery around off, Cook leans across to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. A loud appeal from the bowler but the umpire shakes his head. Chase after having a word with his skipper immediately takes the review. Ultra Edge shows there is no bat involved and the Ball Tracking shows, it's in line and would have gone on to crash the leg stump. A typical Cook innings comes to an end. A nice gesture shown by the Windies players as they go towards the batsman and congratulate him for his spectacular knock.
A huge shout for an LBW against Cook. Not given by Umpire Erasmus. West Indies have taken the review straightaway...
Full around off, defended off the front foot watchfully.
On middle and leg, flicked towards mid-wicket for a single.
Roland-Jones  drives the ball straight down the ground.
Floats it up outside off, Cook crouches low and dabs it pretty late towards short third man where the fielder moves across to his right and dives to stop some runs. A single taken.
Wide delivery outside off, Cook throws his bat at it. Ends up slicing it over a leaping backward point for a single.
Stays back to this length delivery and once again finds the fielder at backward point.
Continues to spray it outside off, making Cook play at it. The batsman couldn't resist this time and decides to go after it. Misses it completely.
Outside off, actually wide outside off, Alastair lifts his bat to leave it alone.
Once again on a similar length and outside off, Alastair flays at it but finds the man at backward point.
Slants it away wide outside off, could have hit it through the line but Cook resists and lets it be.

Drags his length back a touch, punched off the back foot towards Chase. A maiden from the spinner.
Darts it on the stumps, pushed back to the bowler again.
Fuller on the stumps, it's bunted back to the bowler.

A bit flatter and served outside off, Toby dabs it towards point, wants the single but Cook sends him back quickly.
Tossed up around middle, flicked towards the man at short mid-wicket.
A bit fuller outside off, pushed off the front foot towards extra cover.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Good length delivery outside off, punched square of the wicket on the off side for a single.

Fuller and served wide outside off, it's left alone without much fuss.
Bangs in a short ball on middle, Roland-Jones ducks under it safely.

Ali dances down the track to go big down the ground but the ball goes off the splice of the bat and lobs towards backward point where Kraigg Brathwaite nicely settles under that one. The wicket has started to take some turn and that should please Ali as well.
Loopy delivery outside off, Moeen Ali pushes it off the front foot towards cover.
Stays back and pushes it through point for a single.
Around middle and leg, Cook goes back and tucks it into the leg side.
Floats it up around off, Alastair prods forward in defense.
In the channel outside off, Moeen Ali has got nothing to offer.
Ali comes forward and drives it towards mid off.
Moeen Ali is the next man in, replacing Bairstow.

He drops it on a length outside off, Bairstow goes chasing after it but the ball comes back in a touch after hitting the deck, cramps the English keeper for room and that does him in. He gets an inside edge which goes on to disturb the timber. Once again a wicket against the run of play.
Fuller and angling in, Bairstow looks to flick it across the line but closes the face of the bat a bit early and hence gets a safe leading edge towards mid-wicket.

On a back of a length outside off, Bairstow opens the face of the bat and dabs it square of the wicket on the off side for a couple.
Around middle and leg, clipped towards the on side for one.
Roston drops it short again, wide outside off, just a dab towards backward point this time he picks up a single.
Presses forward and keeps it out off the front foot.
FOUR! Uppish but safe! Once again it's quicker through the air, Cook's eyes light up as flays it through backward point again. Finds the fence one more.
Floats it up outside off, defended off the front foot gently.

FOUR! Easily guided! Chase bowls it flat and that too outside off. With no third man in place, Cook decides to take full toll of it. Camps back and guides it through the vacant backward point region for a boundary.

BEATEN! Lands it on a length outside off, Bairstow pokes at it and gets beaten.
Full and outside off, Cook drives it through the covers for a run. That was a beautiful shot for a single.
Full and wide outside off, Cook opens the face of his bat and drives it to point.

Tosses it up outside off, Bairstow does not fiddle with it.
FOUR! DEFT! Bowls it quick outside off, Jonny waits for the ball and plays it late through short third man and the ball races to the fence.

CUTS HIM INTO TWO! Holder goes wide of the crease  and lands it on a length around off, the ball jags in a touch and beats Jonny on the inside and goes through to the keeper.

This session- 27 overs, 101 runs and 1 wicket. Another session which has been dominated by England. Cook and Malan started from where they left off but the wicket of the latter just at the stroke of the break must have given some respite to the Windies. They started off well but could not add to the pressure and thereon run scoring became too easy for the English side. They would want to continue in the same manner and add some quick runs before declaring. When shall that happen? Remains to be seen. Join us in a bit for the second session.

Malan lunges forward to defend but gets an outside edge to first slip where Blackwood makes no mistake. The 162-run stand comes to an end. The youngster has played a fine knock but would be gutted with himself for not making it big. THAT WILL BE LUNCH ON DAY 2!

So what would be the ideal time for Anderson and Broad to have a go with the pink object is what should Root think about, he reckons...

Hello and welcome to the 2nd day of the 1st Test between England and West Indies. The first day panned out how everyone expected it to. The hosts are in a commanding position and with a lot of batting still to come, they would like to bat the visitors out of the game. The Windies, on the other hand would want to make good use of the second new ball and try to trigger a collapse. Let's hope for a better contest between bat and ball. Stay tuned for more updates...
...Day 2, Session 1...

With nothing much on the wicket, expect the hosts to come out and continue to pile up the runs tomorrow morning. If the Windies can't find a way to make a comeback, another long day beckons. Join us at 1400 local (1300 GMT) to catch all the action from day 2. Until then, it's goodbye from us. Cheers!

Once the stand was broken, Dawid Malan stepped in and made sure he wouldn't let this opportunity go to waste. He's gotten his eye in and another partnership has started to bloom. The Windies had a really tough outing and the fact that they gave up towards the end on the very first day, should tell you how difficult the task would pan out for them in the days to come. Apart from Kemar Roach, rest all were way too erratic and didn't create any impact. Leaked a lot of runs and have let the game slip away to say the least.

What a day for England! Alastair Cook, the man of the hour walks back amidst a huge round of applause. He's played an absolute Test innings - full of grit, immense concentration and unflappable temperament. Joe Root couldn't have asked for anything above this. He won a good toss on a batting beauty but then saw two of his batters depart early. He then along with Cook did the resurrection work in a fabulous manner as both of them not only strolled to their respective tons but also accounted for a mammoth 248-run stand which happens to be the highest 3rd wicket partnership at Edgbaston and highest ever in a Day/Night Test.

England have bossed the session. They have managed to score 107 runs in 28 overs without losing a wicket. The experienced duo has continued from where they left off due to some good batting and some wayward bowling from the West Indians. Cook who is unbeaten on 85 and Root who is batting on 103 would want to continue on their merry way. However, the visitors would hope to get some quick wickets to get back in the game. Overdoes his length, bowls it full, Root plays a cover drive, well timed but not well placed. Finds the fielder.
Change in field. Point drops back. That's more like setting a field for poor bowling.
FOUR! Help yourself! Short and wide outside off, Root latches onto it and whacks it through cover-point for a boundary. These are free runs on offer and Joe is collecting them with open arms.
A back foot punch to a shortish ball but straight to the point fielder.
Fullish and on off, driven off the front foot but straight to the mid off fielder.

FOUR! Beautifully done! An overpitched delivery on middle, Cook has no qualms in flicking it through square leg for a boundary. They are bowling too many boundary balls and not letting any pressure build.
Length ball outside off, angling in, Cook remains back and taps it down to covers.
Too full in length and outside off, Cook lunges and pushes it down the ground to mid off.
Four leg byes! Drifting down the leg side, Cook fails to work it across the line but it kisses his hips and runs fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Gentle delivery, full and around off, Cook defends it watchfully to mid on.  Easy going for the English team, not getting tested enough.
Nipping back in from a length outside off, Cook gets across the stumps, closes the face of the bat and keeps it out to mid-wicket.
Fuller and straighter, Root flicks it on the leg side but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Shortish and on off, Root goes back and plays it down to point.

FOUR! Quality shot from a quality batsman! Full in length around off, angling into the batsman, Root gets on the front foot with a vertical bat and caresses it down the ground for a beautiful boundary. Interestingly, this is the first shot played by Root in the V!
On a length around off, angling in, Root gets deep inside the crease and defends it down safely.
Joseph gets away with this bad delivery. Angling down the leg side, full in length, Root fails to get any bat behind it.
Fuller in length and outside off, Root plays a drive away from his body, not much timing and it rolls towards mid off.
FOUR! Easy pickings! Holder bowls five good balls and now slips a length ball on middle and leg, Cook gets across and nudges it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Good delivery but he needs to land it closer to the stumps to make the batsman play. On a fuller length outside off, nipping away, Cook shoulders arms.
Tries to tempt the batsman by offering width outside off, Cook shows a lot of restrain as he allows it through to the keeper.
Slants in a full length ball on off, Cook shuffles across the stumps and defends it to the off side.
Lands it full and outside off, Cook pushes it softly to covers.
Holder runs in from around the wicket and angles in a back of a length ball around off, Cook works it from the crease to square leg.
Shortish in length and outside off, Root steers it off his back foot but fails to pierce the gap on the off side. The cover-point fielder stops the ball with a valiant dive to his left.
Good length delivery in the corridor outside off, Root makes a sensible leave.
That's more like it! Joseph for once gets his line and length right. Pitches it full around off, getting it to move away a shade, Root is sucked into the cover drive but is beaten.

FOUR! On the other side of the wicket this time. Width on offer outside off, Root plays it extremely late and guides it down to third man for a boundary. This is buffet bowling, on both sides of the pitch, really poor from a youngster.
FOUR! Glorious! Joseph digs in a short ball on middle, a gentle pace, 80 mph, Root rides the bounce, swivels inside the crease with his pull shot and nails it in front of square leg for a boundary.
Good length ball on off, angling in, Root sticks to his back foot in defense.
Full and outside off, angling in, Cook once again gets across the stumps a bit and defends it solidly to covers.
Sliding down the leg side, on a good length, Cook gets across the stumps with the flick shot but fails to connect.
FOUR! Holder switches to around the wicket but fails to get the line right. Too straight and Cook tucks it behind square leg for a boundary.
Very full this time, on middle, Cook leans forward and across to flick it through square leg. A couple of runs taken.
Back of a length ball around off, angling away, Cook shoulders arms.
A gentle delivery in the zone outside off, not much bounce, Cook allows it through.
Excellent shot but fails to get the placement right. It's a pitched up ball outside off, Cook plays an elegant drive just wide of extra cover and takes a single.
Around leg, on a length, Cook fails to tuck it off his hips.
Too full and around off, Cook goes for the drive but fails to middle. It rolls back towards the bowler off the inside edge.
Good length ball angling away from the batsman, around off, Cook gets back inside the crease and defends it to the off side.
Goes for a yorker but it reaches the batsman on a low full toss around off, Cook keeps it out to mid off.
Poor beginning to a new spell. Sprays a length ball down the leg side, Cook leaves it.
Alzarri Joseph is back on. He has been very expensive so far and would like to make amends now.
Fuller in length and outside off, driven off the front foot to covers. Not much timing.
Beaten! Good length delivery in the zone outside off, holding its line, Root pushes tamely inside the line and misses.
Full and angling into the batsman, Root pushes it down to mid on.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
31st Test fifty for Joe Root.

FOUR! A flashy shot! Width on offer outside off, short in length as well, Root flashes his blade through the line and it flies down to third man off the outside edge for a boundary. 11th score of 50 or more in succession for him! Run machine, truly.
Starts with a good length ball around off, shaping back in a touch, Root has not much room to play with and taps it down from the back foot to point.
Bowling change. Jason Holder brings himself into the attack.
Full length ball outside off, Cook drives it through the line but finds the mid off fielder.
Angling away from the batsman on a length, Cook leaves it alone.
Great flying stop by Dowrich! Full length ball around leg, swinging down the leg side, Cook fails to flick and Shane dives full length to his right to collect the ball.
Targets the middle stump with a length ball, Cook is squared up a shade as he defends it to the off side.
FOUR! An overpitched ball around leg, Cook is too good a batsman to miss out on a gift. He picks it off his pads and clips it superbly through mid-wicket for a glorious boundary.
Good length ball angling away from the batsman, around off, Cook punches from the crease but finds the point fielder.
FOUR! Poor delivery and punished! A flighted full ball wide outside off, Root gets the chance to free his arms and smashes it  through covers for a boundary. Moves to 47!
Drifting down the leg side, Cook helps it in front of square leg and rotates the strike.
Floated full ball on off, Cook leans forward in defense.
Tossed up ball on middle and leg, turning down, Joe flicks it through backward square leg for one.
Leans forward to a full ball and defends it back.
Loopy off spinner on off, Root plays a stylish flick shot but finds the mid-wicket fielder.
Full and around middle, Cook leans across to flick but it takes the inner half of the bat and rolls towards mid-wicket. Not in the gap and that ends the over.
On a length and around off, Alastair does well to defend it back. That's the line Cummins should concentrate on.
Wild delivery, short and way down the leg side, Cook has nothing to do with it. Cummins has been pretty inconsistent with his lines.
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, Cook goes back and taps it down to mid-wicket
Pitches it full and on off, Root plays a crisp off drive and Cummins uses his left boot to make a partial stop. Deflects it wide of mid off and they cross for a run.
Good length ball on off, Root gets behind the line and defends it back.
Tossed up and outside off, Cook covers the spin and shoulders arms.
Flatter and outside off, Cook allows it through.
A good looking drive by Cook but he finds the fielder at extra cover.
Flighted and on middle, eased through square leg for one.
An off spinner on middle, helped to mid-wicket.
Four leg byes! Turning down the leg side, Root fails to flick and it goes off his pads past short fine leg for a boundary.
A touch short and on middle, jumping onto the batsman, Cook goes on his toes and defends it towards mid-wicket.
Width on offer outside off, Cook plays a cracking square cut from the crease but finds the fielder.
Extra bounce from a length around middle, Cook adjusts well to keep it out towards mid-wicket.
Identical to the last delivery, same region, same length but a little bit of extra bounce, Cook lets it through and Dowrich collects it near his chest.
This time Cummins angles it across the left-hander, on a length and outside off, Cook allows it through.
Wrong line, on a length and down the leg side, Cook tries to flick but fails to connect.
Goes on the back foot and helps it off his pads to mid-wicket.
Flatter this time, on off, Root gets back inside the crease and blocks it safely.
Keeps it tossed up and this time the line is around off, Cook drives it off his front foot to mid off for a single.
A hint of drift on this occasion, landing around off and spinning away a bit, Cook leaves it.
Flatter in the channel outside off, Cook makes a watchful leave.
Chase starts the session with a friendly full toss outside off, Cook fails to put it away and drives it straight to the cover fielder.
Full on middle, Root drives it straight back to the bowler.
A tad shorter outside off, Root tries to force it through the off side but gets beaten.
NO BALL! Lands it on a length outside off, Root does not fiddle with it. A no ball signalled by the umpire as Cummins has overstepped.
Good length angling into the batsman. Root defends it solidly.
A tad fuller outside off, Root does not bother playing at it.
Similar delivery to the last one. Root points his bat skywards and lets it through.
Starts off with a length ball outside off, Root lets it through to the keeper.
We're back for the second session. The umpires are out in the middle. Alastair Cook and Joe Root will continue their innings. Miguel Cummins will bowl the first over after the break.
...Day 1, Session 2...

The Windies on the other hand, have been a little wayward with the ball. Kemar Roach started off well but got little support from the rest. They would want to come out and take a couple of quick wickets or this partnership can take the game away from them. Join us for the second session in a while.

So, England after stuttering a bit at the start have recovered well and made sure the session belonged to them. The hosts, after winning the toss and opting to bat, lost two quick wickets. However, the pair of Joe Root and Alastair Cook has steadied things with the latter registering his 31st Test fifty at home which happens to be the joint most along with Michael Atherton. The home side would hope these two to continue after the break.
Bowls a full toss on off, Cook drives it to short covers. LUNCH ON DAY 1.
Worked towards mid-wicket with the spin for a run.
56th Test fifty for Alastair Cook.

That's a half century for Cook! Full and wide outside off, Cook drives it towards covers where the fielder dives and half stops it. The batsmen take a run. This has been an excellent knock from Alastair.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Fires it outside off, gets some spin away from the batsman. Cook does not bother playing at it.
Flatter outside off, spinning away. Cook shoulders his arms to it.
Bowling change just before the lunch break. Roston Chase to roll his arm over...
FOUR! Through the leg side this time! Full and on the pads, Root flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Root has looked very solid here.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Bowls a yorker on middle, Root does well to dig it out.
Angles it on the pads, Cook flicks it to fine leg for a run.
FOUR! TOP SHOT! Full and wide outside off, Cook drives it through the covers and the ball races to the fence.
LOVELY BOWLING! Lands it on a length on off, nips away off the deck. Cook pokes at it and gets beaten.
Back of a length on middle, Root tucks it towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Not as convincing as the last one. Full and swinging away outside off, Root tries to drive but gets an outside edge through backward point and the ball races to the fence. In the recently concluded series between South Africa and England, Faf du Plessis always had a fielder behind square on the off side for Root as he scores a lot of runs there.
FOUR! Joseph strays on the pads this time. Root camps back and flicks it through the square leg region and the ball races to the fence.
Back of a length on off, Joe pushes it to covers.
Shorter in length outside off, Root does not time his cut shot properly and hits it to point.
Joseph has not got his line right. Bowls it very wide outside off, Root shoulders his arms to it.
50-run stand comes up between the Ex and current English skipper.
Angling into the batsman, Root gets it off the inner half to fine leg for a run.
Good length on off, Root defends it watchfully.
Bowled on off, Root pushes it to covers.
A well-directed bouncer on leg stump, Root is early into the pull shot and hence gets it off the toe end besides the pitch.
A tad fuller on off, Cook lunges forward and pushes it towards cover-point for a run.
Angles it into the batsman from around the wicket. Cook flicks it to mid-wicket.
Good length outside off, swinging away. Root first goes for the cut shot but then pulls out at the last moment.
Short and wide outside off, Root tries to cut but gets a bottom edge to covers. He should have put that away.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Just short of a length outside off, Root pushes it towards the cover fielder.
A tad shorter on off, Root plays a solid looking back foot punch to covers.
Back of a length outside off, Root cuts it towards point.
Alzarri Joseph is called back into the attack.
Bowls an outswinger but way outside off, Cook points his bat skywards and lets it through to the keeper.

Michael Holding on air comes up with a smart point. He says Holder comes steaming in but while delivering the ball, his front foot goes wide which is why he is not able to generate enough pace behind it. Whereas, Kemar Roach while taking his delivery stride has his front foot straight which helps him bowl at a good pace.
A tad fuller on middle, Cook tucks it to mid-wicket.
Goes wider of the crease and fires it full on leg stump, Cook flicks it to mid-wicket.
Good length outside off, Cook lets it through to the keeper.
FOUR! EASY PEASY! Short and angling into the batsman, Cook rocks back and pulls it through square leg for another boundary. He is timing the ball brilliantly.
Starts off with a loosener down the leg side. Cook misses the pull and the ball goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Kemar Roach comes back into the attack.
FOUR! Through the off side this time. Holder bowls it full on the pads, Root leans across and flicks it through mid-wicket and the ball races to the fence. Two boundaries in the over.
Bowls it on the fourth stump line, Root does not bother playing a shot at it.
A tad fuller outside off, Root drives it towards cover for no run.
An inswinger way outside off, Root shoulders his arms to it.
FOUR! WOW! Lovely from Root. Full and outside off, Root leans into it and drives it through covers for boundary.
Back of a length on middle, Root defends it off the back foot.
A tad fuller on off, Cook pushes it off the front foot towards mid off.
Shorter length on off, Cook camps back and pushes it to mid on.
A tad shorter on middle, Cook defends it watchfully.
FOUR! POOR LINE! Short and on off, Cook pushes it off the back foot through point and the ball races to the fence.

Sprays it down the leg side, Cook tries to flick but misses and is collected by the keeper. There is a muted appeal but nothing from the umpire. Replays show that there was daylight between bat and ball.
A tad fuller outside off, Cook shoulders his arms to it.
Bowls it wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Lands it on a length outside off, Root does not bother playing a shot at it.
FOUR! You cannot bowl short to Root, he will hit you all day. Short and gives him width, Root camps back and punches it through the off side for a boundary.
Good length outside off, Root lets it through to the keeper.
A bit short outside off, Joe looks to cut but chops it towards the off side. He looks a bit frustrated out there.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Root off his back foot punches it towards cover. Fails to pierce the gap again.
Comes forward and pushes it back down the wicket.
Slips one down the leg side, Cook tries to help it on its way but fails to do so.
Stays behind the line and punches it towards the mid on fielder.
Back of a length delivery on middle, Alastair tucks it in front of square on the leg side for a single.
Beaten! Rare error from Cook! Cummins slants it away around off, Cook feels for it as he lunges forward to defend but the ball moves away and nearly takes the outside edge towards the keeper.
Good length delivery on off, Cook gets across and with the full face of the bat drives it towards mid on.
A maiden from Holder! Keeps it fuller on off, Root lunges forward and drives it towards the fielder at point.
Angles it in from outside off, it's on a shorter side as Root stays on the back foot and unfurls a punch but straight to extra cover.
On a back of a length, much close to the off stump channel, still Root lifts his bat to let it be.
Good length delivery wide outside off, another easy leave for JR.
Keeps it around off, it moves away. It's too wide to make Root go after it.
Good length delivery outside off, a nice front foot defense on offer.
Once again Miguel Cummins is a bit too straight with his line. It's easily glanced down to fine leg by Root. He'll keep strike.
On the pads, tucked behind square on the leg side for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, Cook stays back and punches it through extra cover and collects a couple to his tally.
After spraying one on the pads, he keeps it outside off. Alastair has nothing to offer.
FOUR! Easily done! A bit short and down the leg side, all Cook has to do is to get some part of wood on it. He does so and the long leg fielder has no chance to cut it off.
On middle and leg, worked towards the man at mid-wicket.
FOUR! Just eased it! Shot! Fuller and it's wide outside off, Root's eyes light up as he leans across and drives it through covers for a boundary. No need to run for those.
Drops it on a fuller length outside off, it comes back in sharply as Root plants his front foot across, covers the sticks and then leaves it alone.
Fuller in length and outside off, Root leans forward to drive but gets an inside edge on the pads as the ball rolls back towards the Windies skipper.
Stays behind the line and keeps it out.
Once again keeps it in the same zone, the English skipper isn't tempted to play at it.
In the corridor of uncertainty, Joe shoulders his arms to that one.
Brings this one back into the left-hander, flicked towards mid-wicket where the fielder dives to his right to deny them the single.
Slants it away on a length outside off, easily left alone by the southpaw.

Edgy! It's on a length outside off, Joe looks to run it down but gets it off the outer half of the bat and it rolls safely towards gully. The man makes a good half-stop and parries it towards point and concedes a run.
Good delivery! Hits the seam near the good length area and then jags away as Root has a tentative poke inside the line. Lucky Root, that the ball didn't kiss the willow.
On a back of a length and served around off, defended off the back foot.
Continues from over the wicket and fires it full on middle and leg, Root prods across and jams it out towards mid on.

Drinks are on the field. England have been rocked early in the first hour itself. Debutant Stoneman and Westley were the wickets to fall but since then the current pair is doing the resurrection job. The Windies bowlers have been right on the money except on a few occasions. If they could get another one here, England would surely be in a spot of bother towards the lunch break. Let's see how they fare in the next hour...
Just ahead of a length on off, Cook defends it by covering the line of the stumps.
Bowls it on a length outside off, the batsman watches it till the last moment and lets it be.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Good length on off, Cook defends it from within the crease.
A tad fuller outside off, Alastair shoulders his arms to it.
Just behind a length on off, Cook defends it to covers.
FOUR! Root plays that shot with a lot of authority. Shorter in length outside off, Root camps back and guides it through backward point for a boundary.
Good length on off, Root defends it solidly.
A tad fuller this time on off, swinging away. Root tries to defend it off the back foot but gets an outside edge to second slip who makes a good diving stop to his right.
Lands it on a length outside off, Root does not bother playing a shot at it.
Back of a length outside off, Root guides it towards point.
Full and wide outside off, Root toe-ends the drive to mid off.
Good length, jags back in. Cook adjusts well and plays it out to covers.
A tad shorter on off, Cook defends it watchfully.

Mike Atherton and his observations are really good. He says Holder has placed a man at extra cover but Cook is such a man, who rarely drives the ball until it's a genuine half-volley. He likes to dab the ball late, so what he suggests is that, remove the man at extra cover and bring him to the slip cordon and there are chances of an edge being induced...

FOUR! Again! He has played this shot four times today and has always fetched a boundary. Back of a length on off, Cook opens the face off his bat and guides it down to third man and the ball races to the fence.
Lands it on a length outside off, Cook shoulders his arms to it.
Full and outside off, Cook drives it square of the wicket on the off side.
Back of a length outside off, Cook guides it towards point.
The skipper brings himself on. It's Jason Holder to have a go with the pink object. Two slips and a gully in place...
Sprays down the leg side, Root misses the flick and the ball is collected by the keeper.
Full on the pads, Cook flicks it beautifully to fine leg for a run.
Good length outside off, Cook watchfully leaves it.
Bowls it on the pads, Cook works it towards mid-wicket.

Sloppy effort in the field! Joseph is the culprit. Full on middle, Root times it towards mid on. Alzarri stationed at short mid-wicket runs to his left, dives over the ball and lets it through. The fielder from mid off gives it a chase and stops the ball just inside the rope to save a run for his side.
Very full on off, Root jams it out towards covers.
Full and wide outside off, Cook points his bat skywards and lets it through to the keeper.
WIDE! Don't see too many bowled in a Test match. Bowls it short outside off, Cook lets it through and the umpire signals a wide. Second by Roach.
Good length on off, Root taps it on the off side and the batsmen run through for a single.
Beaten for pace! Bowls it on a length on middle, Root tries to defend it but is late on it and gets hit high on the pads.
A tad shorter on leg stump, Cook pushes it through mid on for a run.
Lands it on a length outside off, Cook tries to defend inside the line but gets beaten.
Bowls it just outside off, Cook watches it well and makes a good leave.
Back of a length outside off, Root cuts it to point.
Lands it on a length on middle, Root defends it watchfully.
Good length outside off, Root lets it through to the keeper.
The English skipper, Joe Root is in next.

OUT! A brilliant, brilliant review by West Indies. What a start for them. They have their second. Full ball outside off shaping in, Westley misses the flick and is struck on the pads. The Windies appeal and the umpire shakes his head. After a chat with his teammates, Holder decides to review and they go upstairs. The front foot is fine. There is no inside edge. The ball is pitching in line, has struck him in line and is going on to hit the leg stump. Three reds and the decision has to be overturned. A great bowling change by Holder.
Howzzaattt? Is the shout from the bowler. It looks close to the naked eye. Jason Holder has taken the review. Is there an inside edge? Let's wait and find out...
A tad fuller outside off, shaping away. Tom watchfully lets it through to the keeper.
Starts off with a loosner outside off, Westley shoulders his arms to it.
Miguel Cummins comes into the attack.
Similar length, Cook again lets it through to the keeper. A maiden for Roach.
Bowls it outside off, the batsman leaves it watchfully.

Nasser Hussain on air informs that - it's only the second time in this season that Mark Stoneman has been  bowled. He's in good form of late but unfortunately, he got a peach of a delivery which led to his undoing...
A tad fuller outside off, Cook shoulders his arms to it.
Good lines and lengths here from Roach! Lands it on a length on middle, Alastair lunges forward and defends it towards mid on.
Good length outside off, Cook lets it through to the keeper.
Back of a length on middle, Cook tries to work it on the leg side but gets a soft leading edge towards cover-point.
Bowls an inswinger this time on the pads, Westley flicks it straight to square leg.
Full and swinging away outside off, Tom points his bat skyward and lets it through to the keeper.
FOUR! It is raining boundaries here. A tad short outside off, Westley rocks back and punches it through covers and the ball races to the fence.
Wide enough for the batsman to not play at it.
Back of a length on off, Cook pushes it through the covers for a run.
FOUR! He plays that shot to great effect. Lands it on a length on off, Cook guides it through the slip cordon for another boundary. Cook is off to a brisk start here.
Full on middle, Westley tries to flick it but gets a safe leading edge to mid on.
Good length outside off, the batsman does not bother playing a shot at it.
Bowls it on a length on off, Tom defends it by covering the line of the ball.
BEAUTY! Good length on off, nipping away. Westley tries to poke at it but gets beaten.
Back of a length on off, Westley defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! TOP SHOT! Full and on middle, Westley drives it straight back past the bowler and the ball races to the fence. Tom gets off the mark with that boundary.
FOUR! Short and outside off, Cook cuts it through gully for another boundary.
FOUR! He is dealing in boundaries! Full and outside off, Cook drives it through covers and the ball races to the fence.
A tad shorter on off, Cook camps back and defends it.
Good length on off, Cook defends it watchfully.
A tad shorter outside off, Cook square cuts it to point.
FOUR! You can't bowl on this guy's pads. Cook flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
RIPPER! Length on off, shaping away. Westley tries to defend it but gets beaten. What an over from Roach. Top notch.
Lands it outside off, Westley shoulders his arms to it.
Full on middle, Westley drives it to mid on.
Full and wide outside off, Tom lets it through to the keeper.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Tom Westley is the next man in.

OUT! KABOOM! What a jaffa! How do you play that one? Lands it on a length around leg stump, nips away a touch. Stoneman tries to defend it but gets beaten and the ball hits the top of off. What a return for Kemar Roach! A wayward first over but he has started this one in explicable fashion. Stoneman the debutant has to depart, not a good outing for him. The opening issues for England continue.
Fullish on middle, Cook drives it straight but the ball hits the stumps at the non-striker's end and deflects to mid on.
Back of a length outside off, Cook tries to cut but gets a bottom edge onto the ground and the ball rolls towards the off side.
FOUR! This outfield is lightning quick! Lands it on a length on off, Cook opens the face of his bat and guides it down to third man for another boundary.
Fuller in length on off, Cook defends it off the front foot.
Sprays it down the leg side, Cook misses the flick and it goes through to the keeper. There was not a lot of carry there for the bowler.
A tad fuller outside off, Cook does not bother playing a shot at it.
Alzarri Joseph will bowl from the other end.
Lands it on a length outside off, Stoneman shoulders his arms to it. A good start for Mark.
FOUR! No nerves for this guy! Full and on the pads, Stoneman flicks it through square leg and the ball races to the fence. Second boundary for Stoneman in the space of three balls.
Good length on off, Mark lunges forward and defends it solidly.

FOUR! First runs for Stoneman in Test cricket! What a way to get off the mark. Full and outside off, Stoneman leans into it and drives it through covers for a boundary. That was a lovely shot from the debutant.
Lands it on a length outside off, Stoneman lets it through to the keeper.
WIDE! What was that? Full and very, very wide outside off. The batsman lets it through and the fielder at second slip does well to stop it. The umpire signals a wide.
Starts off with a length ball on off, Cook taps it in front of covers for a run. England have their first run. Cook gets off the mark.

We are ready to get underway. The players and the umpires are out in the middle. Alastair Cook and Mark Stoneman will open the batting for England. Kemar Roach will open the bowling for West Indies. He has three slips and a gully in place for him.

TOSS - ENGLAND WIN THE TOSS AND OPT TO BAT! Debuts for both the sides. MARK STONEMAN for England and it's KYLE HOPE for the Windies. The former will open the batting for the hosts while the latter had a good time in the warm-up game, scoring a ton. Come this game, both will look to build on the platform that is on offer.

As is the case, when there is West Indies playing in white attire, chances of the game being lopsided rises. However, they already have experienced this flavor before and with a good bowling attack, they would expect to come good. The weather in this part of the world is highly unpredictable, so let's hope that it doesn't play spoilsport. Which team will come out on top? Stay with us to see how things unfold. Toss and team news coming up in a bit...

Hello and a warm welcome for the first Test match between England and the Windies at Edgbaston. It's going to be a historic one in all likelihood as this shall be the 50th game and the very first Day/Night Test to be played in the country. The hosts though have never tasted how the pink ball plays but one would argue they have the sources to counter it well.
